newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity settles lower on weather, hydro.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity settles lower on weather, hydro.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled sharply lower Monday, erasing early gains on forecasts of warm weather and growing concerns over accelerated rate of snowmelt in the Pacific Northwest.
"People are looking for that first big runoff," said one New York paper broker.
Brokers said the mild weather outlook in the West and worries of high spring runoffs to the vast hydroelectric dams overshadowed news of ongoing plant outages in the Southwest.

In the Pacific Northwest, a series of low pressure systems would continue to bring precipitation along the coast over the next several days. Temperatures would run 14 degrees Fahrenheit above normal in the extreme southeast to about four degrees above normal in the northwest.
In the Southwest, readings would average about 14 degrees above normal in the northeast as well as in the southern deserts to about five degrees above normal in the extreme northwest.
"In the forwards market, people believe the worse has happened," the broker said, noting the reverse of the uptrend of power futures, which began this month.

While scattered plant outages kept spot cash power prices steady in the West, one of larger outages, the 1,070 megawatt (MW) San Onofre nuclear unit 2 is expected to restart Thursday and reach full output this weekend.
April California-Oregon Border (COB) ended down 95 cents at $10.93 a megawatt hour (MWh) after posting a session high of $12.20 in early trading.
May COB settled down 85 cents at $10.00. Other COB months finished 10 to 45 cents lower.
April Palo Verde (PV) ended down 94 cents at $14.83 after traded between $14.70 and $16.05.
May PV settled down 52 cents at $16.65. Other active PV contracts finished 10 to 50 cents lower.
"You have gas (futures) lower. It's cool enough that you don't have AC (air conditioning) demand in the Southwest," said a New York futures broker.
NYMEX April Henry Hub natural gas futures finished down 5.1 cents at $1.909 per million British thermal units.
With a major shift in market sentiment, market sources said they expect the electricity complex to continue today's decline Tuesday.
NYMEX estimated 294 COB and 275 PV contracts were sold, compared with 181 COB and 463 PV lots Friday.
